newsitem.title: USA: Kiwi Intl in debtor-in-possession talks.
newsitem.headline: Kiwi Intl in debtor-in-possession talks.

text.p: Kiwi International Air Lines is presently negotiating with three possible backers for the bankrupt airline's debtor-in-possession financing, said Rob Kulat, a company spokesman.
Kulat said one of the possible backers is Victor Kiam II, who is best known for owning Remington Products Co, and the two other parties were not disclosed. Kiam could not be reached for comment.
Kiwi is scheduled to appear in U.S. Bankruptcy Court in Newark, N.J., October 15, with a proposal for debtor-in-possession financing, Kulat said.
Kiam's proposal was for $2 million, a figure Kulat said "would be adequate to continue operations."
Kiwi's employees would have the opportunity to participate in the other $2 million in financing, Kulat said.
Kiwi, which declared bankruptcy on September 30, 1996, cut its schedule back to three cities with 24 daily flights, shedding routes to Las Vegas, Florida, and Bermuda.
Prior to the filing it had 63 daily flights, Kulat said.
